requirements.requirement: Record commands run through sudo on node1 in /var/log/sudo-commands.log, including the invoking user and timestamp.
requirements.summary: A validated sudoers policy directs sudo logging to the required file and enables four-digit years. Direct pre- and post-reboot tests produced entries containing timestamps, invoking user root, run-as user nobody, working directory, and command. The file was root-owned, mode 0600, and correctly SELinux-labeled.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log.
requirements.summary: The policy disables sudo syslog output. Unique test commands appeared in the dedicated log while matching counts across /var/log/messages, /var/log/secure, and the relevant journal windows were zero both before and after reboot.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged the scheduled reboot, became temporarily unreachable, returned with a different boot identity, and retained valid configuration, prior log data, active logging services, and correct new-command behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Behavior was sampled with two representative successful sudo commands rather than every possible sudo command form; the validated global sudoers defaults provide strong supporting coverage.
The invoking-user field was directly demonstrated for root only, although the entry format clearly records that identity and separately records the run-as user.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the sudoers drop-in was the required implementation (cmd-a66a071ad1f34bbd); the sudo invocations were bounded functional checks, and the scheduled reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. No failed services, package damage, new exposure, or abandoned non-system temporary files were observed afterward. Socket and systemd-private-directory differences are normal consequences of the verified reboot.
